title: 6810M12/CTL: Glanaber, Main Street, Llwyngwril, LL37 2YQ
text:
TRIBIWNLYS PRISIO CYMRU - VALUATION TRIBUNAL FOR WALES

COUNCIL TAX DECISION

Page 1 of 5

Appellant: Mr M Walker

Appeal Number:  6810M12/CTL/1

Appellant’s Address: Glanaber, Main Streert, Llwyngwril LL37 2YQ

The Matter Appealed against:  Council Tax Liability Appeal

Date of Hearing: 30 May 2019

Appearances:  Mrs B Rees Gwynedd Council (GC)

Date of Decision:    17 June 2019

Decision of Tribunal:  Appeal Allowed

Members of the Tribunal:
Mr Rh Prytherch

Mr C Newman
Ms M Griffith

Tribunal Clerk: Mrs C Jones

Introduction:

1. The appellant appealed against GC’s refusal to grant him Single Person
Discount (SPD) in respect of the property Glanaber, Main Street,
Llwyngwyril.

2. This is a summary of the case and is not intended to be an exhaustive
record of the proceedings. However, the parties can be assured all the
evidence was fully considered by the Tribunal when it arrived at its
decision. Consequently, the absence of reference to any statement, or
evidence, should not be construed as being overlooked.

Summary of the Appellant’s Evidence

3. The Clerk explained that the appellant was not present and had submitted
a written submission, to read to the Tribunal in his absence.  The Clerk
then read out relevant details from the appeal form and the written
submission as reproduced below;

Extract
“I live in Llwyngwril full-time.  I own jointly with my wife, Jill Walker, two
other properties.  32 Plas Panteidal, Aberdovey, LL35 0RF is a self-
catering holiday let and 14 Hillaries Road, Erdington, Birmingham is an
HMO divided into 6 rooms with shared facilities.  No. 32 has business
rates applied and full Council Tax is paid at No 14.  Gwynedd Council
accept I live in Llwyngwril alone but say that because I am married, it is
expected that I live with my wife at No14.  It is deemed our family home.

COUNCIL TAX DECISION

Page 2 of 5
My wife works full time in Birmingham and lives at No 14 as a live-in
landlord.  I spend 0% time at No 32 and No 14 Hillaries Road will not be a
family home for me or anyone else in the future.  I will never live there
again, and my wife can’t wait to retire in roughly 2 years’ time and move to
Llwyngwril.  My GP and Dentist are in Gwynedd (Tywyn and Dolgellau).  I
vote in Gwynedd.  I run a B&B in Gwynedd.  www.glanaberbnb.co.uk  I
am 6 years older than my wife, so pension rules differ.  My wife’s GP,
Dentist, voting and banking are in Birmingham – she works and lives
there.  My banking, pensions and tax affairs are in Gwynedd.  I know this
situation is unusual, but it is genuine and temporary.  Thanks for
considering this application for Council Tax single person reduction.

………I have received a pack of information from the Council today.   I
would be grateful if this email could also be shared with the valuation
tribunal.  I have guests staying at the B&B so am unable to attend.

The Council have quoted case law that does not apply to my
situation.  The marital main residence ended in January 2016 when work
began to convert 14 Hillaries Road into an HMO.  Tenants moved in to No
14 in August 2016 and it became a small HMO with 4 unrelated people
living there.  On 1 November 2018 it became a licensed HMO with 6
unrelated people living there.

I move that the marital main residence cannot be deemed as No 14 due
to the change of use.  The marital main residence has not been re-
established and can only be done when Mrs Walker moves to Glanaber in
the near future.”

Summary of the Billing Authority’s Evidence

4. Mrs Rees on behalf of GC distributed her evidence pack to the Tribunal
which contained the following: -

• Skeleton Argument
• Supporting Evidence: -
o Appendix 1 - Land Registry entry - Glanaber, Llwyngwril
o Appendix 2 - Land Registry entry – 14 Hillaries Road, Erdington
o Appendix 3 - Cox v London South West Valuation Tribunal HC
(RVR 1994 171)
o Appendix 4 – SI 2015/2068 The Council Tax (Exceptions to
Higher Amounts) (Wales) Regulations 2015

5. Mrs Rees said that Mr Walker had been registered for Council Tax liability
at Glanaber, Llwyngwril since the 14 August 2015 together with Mrs Jill
Walker.  Mr and Mrs Walker also jointly owned the leasehold of 14 Hillaries
Road, Erdington, Birmingham.

6. Mrs Rees explained that in accordance with the Local Government Finance
Act 1992 if there was only one-person resident in the property, as their sole

COUNCIL TAX DECISION

Page 3 of 5
or main residence, a discount of 25% was applicable.  GC contended that
as this discount could only be applied to a person’s sole or main residence,
it was important to look at the sole or main residence of both Mr and Mrs
Walker and to consider relevant case law.

7. Mrs Rees quoted the case of Cox v London South West Valuation and
Community Charge Tribunal and Poole Borough Council Community
Charge Registration Officer 1994 as relevant to the appeal.  The
taxpayer spent time at two dwellings.  The High Court concluded that the
sole or main residence was the home where the wife and family resided.  It
was GC’s contention that as Mr and Mrs Walker remained in a marital
relationship it would follow, in line with the Cox v London South West case,
that either Glanaber or 14 Hillaries Road would be the sole or main
residence of both parties as the marital home.  Mr and Mrs Walker were
joint owners of both properties, therefore had security of tenure at both
addresses.

8. Mrs Rees stated that Mrs Walker had never had her sole or main residence
at the Llwyngwril address and therefore it was reasonable to assume the
marital home remained to be 14 Hillaries Road as the sole or main
residence of both Mr and Mrs Walker.  Mrs Rees acknowledged Mrs
Walker’s intention to move to Llwyngwril in a couple of years when she
retired.

9. She clarified that Mr Walker resided at the Llwyngwril as he ran a Bed and
Breakfast business from that property and consequently was required to be
on site for his guests.  This would mean that Glanaber could be a second
property, but it qualified for exception to the premium charge as a job-
related hereditament under Class 7 of SI 2015/2068 (the Council Tax
(Exceptions to Higher Amounts) (Wales) Regulations) until such time as
Mrs Walker retired and moved to Llwyngwril.

10. In conclusion of her evidence Mrs Rees said that as Mr and Mrs Walker
remained in a marital relationship, for the purposes of Council Tax and in
consideration of Council Tax case law, their sole or main residence should
be together at the same address.  It was GC’s belief that in this instance it
was reasonable to assume that this remained to be 14 Hillaries Road until
Mrs Walker ceased employment and completed the move to reside
permanently at Llwyngwril in the future.  She requested that the appeal be
dismissed.

11. At the conclusion of the hearing the Tribunal decided to reserve its
decision.

The Reasons for Decision

12. Having considered all the evidence placed before it, both written and oral,
the Tribunal decided to allow the appeal for the following reasons.

COUNCIL TAX DECISION

Page 4 of 5
13. Under the prevailing Legislation the Tribunal had to determine which
property was Mr Walker’s ‘main residence’.  It had regard to the hierarchy of
liability under Section 6 of the LGFA 1992 and concluded that a person can
only have their sole or main residence at one address.

14. Section 6(5) of the Local Government Finance Act 1992 defines the ‘resident’
of a dwelling as being an individual who has attained the age of 18 and has
his, or her, sole or main residence there. The term ‘sole or main residence’
was not defined under Statute; therefore, the Tribunal had regard to
judgements of the higher Courts in which the concept of sole or main
residence had been rehearsed on previous occasions.

15. Looking to the case law provided by the Billing Authority, the Tribunal
accepted that there were similarities.  However, unlike the Cox v London
case, in this case it was not the husband who stayed at a property due to
work commitments, but the wife.

16. The Tribunal believed that a marital home could be established elsewhere,
if the appellants chose to do so, keeping the original property for the
partner’s work commitments.

17. Focusing on the material facts of Mr Walker’ situation, the Tribunal concluded
that he had stronger links to the Llwyngwril property.  He ran a bed and
breakfast business there, so he had work links there.  He had no work links
to the Birmingham address.    Mr Walker’s driving licence was registered to
the Llwyngwril address as was his bank account.  He was registered with a
Doctor and Dentist and registered to vote in Gwynedd.  Mr Walker had
indicated that he had no intention of returning to live at his former marital
home in Birmingham.  This fact was supported by the conversion of this
property into a registered house in multiple occupation.  The intention was
for Mrs Walker to retire to the Llwyngwril address and join her husband within
the next two years.

18. In the Tribunal’s opinion, whilst 4 Hillaries Road was previously the couple’s
matrimonial home and where his wife continued to live, the property was now
an HMO and occupied by several other residents.

19. The Tribunal, in the absence of any other argument, accepted that Mr
Walker intended to stay at the Llwyngwril address.  It was accepted that he
spent all his time at Llwyngwril.

20. Based on the balance of probability the Tribunal felt the Mr Walker’s sole or
main residence lay in Gwynedd, and not in Birmingham.

21. Looking to the scope of the appeal the Tribunal felt that it had no remit,
under this appeal, to decide on Mrs Walker’s sole or main residence.  The
matter under consideration was whether Gwynedd Council had acted
correctly in denying Mr Walker the Single Person’s Discount at the
Llwyngwril address.

COUNCIL TAX DECISION

Page 5 of 5
22. Considering the above, the Tribunal concluded that Mr Walker’s work and
financial links together with the pattern of family life would indicate that
Glanaber, Main Streert, Llwyngwril was the appellant’s ‘main residence’.
Therefore, Gwynedd Council were incorrect in refusing the Single Person’s
Discount.

Certified a true copy on  17 June 2019
